quarterly_data.signal: CFO Bren Higgins on services (pure service, no systems inside): KLA has 'an updated target growth model of 13%-15% moving forward', and '80% is contract-based, so subscription-like in a lot of ways', with an operating margin profile accretive to the company and 'only had one down year, I think, in 25 years'. The 13%-15% target was laid out in March on a five-year industry view, and 'that view looks conservative today', which he says creates an opportunity to drive more growth out of service as more systems ship. (The 'mid-teens' wording in the question was the moderator's.)
quarterly_data.figure: 80% is contract-based; that view looks conservative today

quarterly_data.signal: Optical vs e-beam inspection split: 'historically, it has been about 80/20', and today 'it is probably a little bit higher in the higher end of the maybe 85% plus' on the optical side, driven by the relative growth rates of the two markets. E-beam is inherently slow and used in production only for defect types it alone can find; Higgins expects high-end optical pattern inspection to be one of the fastest-growing markets in process control and does not think the ratio changes much going forward.
